narrative:
The 2018 Texas Rangers entered the season with fading playoff hopes and a roster in transition, and what followed was a long, grinding descent toward a 67-95 finish. The pitching staff was a chronic problem all year, surrendering 848 runs and posting a 4.92 ERA, and the offense — while capable of the occasional explosive moment — could never sustain enough momentum to compensate. The early months hinted at competitiveness, but the team never truly threatened above .500 for any meaningful stretch.

May offered the season's most memorable offensive fireworks, with Joey Gallo's towering home runs, Nomar Mazara's clutch shot, and a wild pair of games on May 23rd in which Ronald Guzman and Jurickson Profar delivered huge hits. Yet even in those weeks, the bullpen was already cracking — Keone Kela surrendered a punishing Michael Brantley grand slam on May 1st that encapsulated the team's fragility in close games. June brought the best winning stretch of the year at 14-11, sustained by moments like Jose Trevino's improbable walk-off single in mid-June.

July marked the true turning point where the season began to unravel. An 8-17 record told the story plainly, punctuated by back-to-back disasters against Oakland — Khris Davis slugging a three-run bomb off Austin Bibens-Dirkx on July 24th and then a walk-off two-run shot off José Leclerc the very next night, a gut-punch sequence that epitomized the Rangers' inability to hold leads. Even Shin-Soo Choo's three-run homer on July 30th couldn't paper over another late-game collapse against Arizona that same day.

The final two months were a slow fade into irrelevance. August produced a 12-14 mark propped up by Rougned Odor's back-to-back multi-run home runs but undermined by a defense and rotation that kept leaking runs. September collapsed entirely at 9-18, with Jeffrey Springs surrendering a killing double in mid-September and Matt Moore yielding a late-season homer in the season's final weeks. The Rangers finished the year 28 games under .500, a franchise clearly in need of a rebuild heading into the offseason.

chapters.title: Early Cracks, Early Sparks
chapters.description: May's offensive explosions are undercut immediately by a devastating bullpen grand slam, previewing the Rangers' fatal inconsistency.

chapters.title: The May Surge
chapters.description: Back-to-back high-leverage hits from Guzman and Profar highlight a productive stretch that briefly makes the Rangers look dangerous.

chapters.title: A June to Remember
chapters.description: Jose Trevino's unlikely bases-clearing single caps the Rangers' best month, a 14-11 record that represents the season's high-water mark.

chapters.title: Oakland Breaks Them
chapters.description: Khris Davis destroys the Rangers on back-to-back nights in late July, punctuating an 8-17 collapse that ends any remaining hope.

chapters.title: Odor's Last Stand
chapters.description: Rougned Odor delivers a pair of multi-run home runs in August to keep things interesting, but the losses keep piling up around him.

chapters.title: Fading Into September
chapters.description: A 9-18 September record seals a lost season, with late-game collapses and yielded home runs defining the Rangers' painful finish.
